compiled_state.title: ticket link: add redundant transitive depends_on edge -> 'would create a cycle' rejection
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** bb326ae95589f5fc796f922b5e47b792745795e2
* **Plugin/Tool Versions:** dso-dev 1.16.11
* **Context Scope:** Worktree session running /dso:preplanning across 4 epics (188c-47e4, d765-a3b6, 8623-8d6a, c206-5acb); cycle errors emerged during dependency wiring after adversarial-review surviving findings were applied.

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

`.claude/scripts/dso ticket link <src> <tgt> depends_on` should accept any edge that does not produce a directed cycle. A redundant edge — one whose endpoints are already transitively connected in the same direction (A reaches B via A -> X -> B) — is not a cycle and should either be accepted as a no-op or accepted as an explicit redundant edge. A cycle exists only when adding A -> B creates a path B -> ... -> A.

#### Actual Behavior

Three distinct edges were rejected with `Error: Adding <src> -> <tgt> (depends_on) would create a cycle` despite no observable reverse path existing in the data:

1. Epic A2 (8623-8d6a-0bc1-4c6e), attempting `ticket link 9143-eab3-6390-4e6a c6da-6632-a3b7-4dcf depends_on` (S7 posture-writer -> S3 prompts/strata dir). S3 was created before S7 and no link from S3 to S7 (or via any intermediary back to S7) had been issued.
2. Epic A2, attempting `ticket link 35cd-5e35-2e0e-4d19 c11d-b0fe-013a-47b0 depends_on` (S5 arch-enforcement -> S2 detect-strata.sh). S2 was created before S5; only S5 -> S1 (RED) had been linked previously; no path from S2 to S5 had been created.
3. Epic B (c206-5acb-9c69-4612), attempting `ticket link 873e-ce1b-6d98-419e b2a1-0d45-e5b6-4856 depends_on` (S5 preplanning -> S4 brainstorm). The same edge had been created earlier in the same session by the dependency-wiring loop, so this third occurrence may be a duplicate-rejection misreporting itself as a cycle; however, occurrences (1) and (2) cannot be explained by duplication and remain unexplained.

### 3. Action History and Workarounds

* **Steps Taken:**
  * Created stories for each epic via `ticket create story --parent=<epic>` in batch.
  * Wired dependencies via `ticket link <impl> <blocker> depends_on` in loops, then issued additional links from adversarial-review findings.
* **Raw Results:**
  * `Error: Adding 9143-eab3-6390-4e6a -> c6da-6632-a3b7-4dcf (depends_on) would create a cycle`
  * `Error: Adding 35cd-5e35-2e0e-4d19 -> c11d-b0fe-013a-47b0 (depends_on) would create a cycle`
  * `Error: Adding 873e-ce1b-6d98-419e -> b2a1-0d45-e5b6-4856 (depends_on) would create a cycle`
* **Known Workarounds:** Skip the rejected edge — downstream `ticket deps` shows the desired ordering is preserved transitively. The rejection blocked an intended explicit edge but did not break the dependency graph in any of the three cases.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* **Active Workflow:** `/dso:preplanning` Phase 4 dependency wiring + Phase 2.5 adversarial-review finding application (add_dependency type)

comments.body: Fixed: check_would_create_cycle() in ticket_graph/_graph.py incorrectly used _get_all_blocked_by(target) for both 'blocks' and 'depends_on' relations. For 'depends_on', the cycle check must use _get_all_blocked_by(source) and check if target is in the result — not _get_all_blocked_by(target) checking for source. The prior code traversed depends_on edges backward, incorrectly treating A→C→B as a cycle when A→B was proposed. Fix: for relation=='depends_on', swap the lookup to _get_all_blocked_by(source_id) and check target_id in result. Two regression tests added to test_ticket_graph.py: test_check_would_create_cycle_no_false_positive_for_transitive_depends_on and test_add_dependency_allows_redundant_transitive_depends_on. All 49 existing tests continue to pass.
